taxonomic_note: Legacy Master Plant Pool name Chamaesyce fendleri is normalized to the current accepted Euphorbia name.
look_here_first: Think low perennial, not tiny annual mat. E. fendleri arises in dense clusters from a woody, thickened taproot/crown and has glabrous stems, small entire rounded leaves, and distinct narrow-linear stipules. Confirm with the glabrous depressed-globose capsule and relatively large white 4-angled seed.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays-local legacy Chamaesyce source; current Kew explicitly treats Chamaesyce fendleri as a synonym of Euphorbia fendleri.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Installed for active visual learning; broader exact-county reconciliation deferred.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Euphorbia sect. Anisophyllum sandmat. Habit longevity, stipules, leaf margins, capsule surface, and seed form are more reliable than gland-appendage shape.
morphology_keys.growth_form: Perennial with woody, thickened taproot; stems usually prostrate, decumbent, or ascending, very rarely erect, densely clustered from the woody crown, about 5–12 cm.
morphology_keys.leaves: Usually opposite, rarely whorled; blades typically orbiculate to ovate, rarely almost lanceolate, about 3–8 × 2.5–7 mm; base slightly asymmetric and slightly cordate to rounded/obtuse; margins entire; surfaces glabrous.
morphology_keys.stipules: Distinct, narrowly linear, about 0.5–1 mm, glabrous.
morphology_keys.cyathium: Solitary at distal nodes. Four yellow-green to reddish glands; appendages absent or white/pink and highly variable in size/shape, so appendage form should not be used as a primary ID character.
morphology_keys.seed: Seeds white, ovoid-pyramidal, prominently 4-angled in cross section, about 1.7–2 × 1–1.2 mm, smooth to slightly wrinkled.
best_field_traits: dense cluster of very low glabrous stems
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Against the tiny annual sandmats, the woody perennial base is a major clue. Against E. angusta, E. fendleri stays low and has short rounded leaves; E. angusta is erect with very narrow distal leaves. Do not lean heavily on involucral gland appendage shape because it is variable in E. fendleri.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Woody perennial crown + low glabrous clustered stems + tiny entire rounded leaves + linear stipules is the strongest field package.

lookalike_matrix.Euphorbia villifera: annual or perennial; sometimes woody rootstock

lookalike_matrix.Euphorbia fendleri: 5–12 cm, usually prostrate/decumbent/ascending in dense crown cluster

lookalike_matrix.Euphorbia angusta: distal leaves linear, >6× as long as wide

unreliable_characters: gland appendage presence, size, or shape by itself
